_comment: WC2026 SEMI-FINAL (M102: England, QF99 winner, vs Argentina, QF100 winner) -- the CHAOS semi: the two most open, goal-laden profiles left, the stylistic opposite of France-Spain. Nominal bracket orientation is England (home, feeder 99) vs Argentina (away, feeder 100); modelled here with ARGENTINA as home (the favourite) -- immaterial on a neutral venue; the web app flips. MEASURED PROFILES (7 matches each): ARGENTINA (rating 95) -- GF 17 / GA 6; scored THREE in every knockout (3-2 aet, 3-2, 3-1 aet), CONCEDED in every knockout, went deep in two of three; reliable advancement, chaotic texture (the team-specific note, now 3-for-3). ENGLAND (rating 91) -- GF 13 / GA 6; real attack (Kane firing all tournament), leaky defence, BTTS-Yes in 5 of 7, open games (4-2, 3-2, 2-1, 2-1 aet), just survived extra time vs Norway. Class gap ~4 -> Argentina the slight-to-moderate favourite. NOTE: the new tie-breaker rule (break toward the elite defence) does NOT apply -- NEITHER side has an elite defence (both GA 6); this tie is broken on class + firepower, which point the same way (Argentina). Texture: both profiles scream GOALS -- total 2.80, Over 2.5 53%, BTTS-Yes 57% (England scored in 6 of 7; Argentina concedes every knockout), clean sheets LOW (29.5% / 20.6%). Deep tail honest (ET 26.5%, pens 13.1%) -- both sides just played extra time. CONCLUSIVE BOTTOM LINE (graded strictly): THE CALL -- Argentina advance IN 90 MINUTES in an open, both-score game (moderate edge: 59.2/40.8). THE SCORELINE -- Argentina 2-1 (2nd modal at 9.3% and the profile-consistent pick: Argentina always scores 2-3, England always scores). THE MARKETS -- 1X2: Argentina (44.9 vs 28.6); Over 2.5: YES (thin, 53.1%); BTTS: YES (56.8%). Risk: both teams' deep tendencies -- if level late, the 26.5% ET branch spoils the manner; and Kane vs Argentina's soft defence can flip a knife-edge game outright. Home = Argentina (nominal; bracket shows England as home). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

market._source: REAL Bet365 line supplied by the user on matchday (screenshot, 1X2 90'): England 2.70 / Draw 2.87 / Argentina 3.00. Replaces the earlier ESTIMATED line [2.10,3.40,3.40].

_recal: MAJOR RECALIBRATION on real market data. My original line was an ESTIMATE (Argentina 2.10 / 3.40 / 3.40 -> ARG 44.7 de-vig) built from ratings+form; the user supplied the REAL Bet365 board: England 2.70 / Draw 2.87 / Argentina 3.00 -> de-vig ENG 35.2 / Draw 33.1 / ARG 31.7. Two big corrections: (1) the FAVOURITE FLIPS -- the real market makes England the thin favourite (England's harder run: eliminated host Mexico and Haaland's Norway; Argentina's accumulated fatigue: two extra-times and a 2-0-down comeback; form quality over rating prior); (2) the DRAW IS FAT (33.1% -- a 2.87 draw is very short) -> the market expects a TIGHT, CAGEY, LOW-scoring semi (total ~2.0), NOT the open goal-fest my profile read suggested. Realigned lambdas ARG 1.58->0.95 / ENG 1.22->1.02 (div 0.1). DISSENT DECLARED: my measured profiles (Argentina scored 3 in every knockout and concedes in all; England BTTS-Yes in 5 of 7) argue for more goals than this line implies -- but per the standing discipline the market wins on side and magnitude; the dissent is recorded, not acted on. Advancement now England 52.1 / Argentina 47.9 (was Argentina 59.2). ET 33.0%, pens 19.3% -- the deepest tie of the tournament.
_validation: 3 seeds x 500k Monte Carlo on the REAL-market calibration (0.95/1.02): worst diff across 8 metrics and 3 seeds = 0.17 pts -- fully converged. Earlier battery on the estimated line superseded.

_bottom_line.call: RE-ISSUED on the real Bet365 line (the original Argentina call is void -- it was built on my estimated odds). England advance, most likely IN 90 MINUTES, in a TIGHT, cagey, low-scoring semi -- razor-thin edge (52.1/47.9) with the tournament's fattest deep tail (ET 33%, pens 19%).
_bottom_line.risk: This is the closest call of the tournament: the 33% extra-time branch is the single likeliest manner-spoiler, 19% reaches penalties (near-coin-flip), and my own profile evidence (Argentina scored 3 in every knockout; England BTTS-Yes in 5 of 7) dissents toward more goals than the market line implies -- if the game opens up, the Under/BTTS-No legs break first.

_postmatch.result: Argentina 2-1 England, settled in 90'. ARGENTINA advance to the FINAL vs Spain; England go to the third-place match vs France.
_postmatch.model_1x2: Final calibration (real Bet365 line): Argentina 31.7 / Draw 33.0 / England 35.3 (LOW); advancement England 52.1 / Argentina 47.9. BINDING BOTTOM LINE (re-issued): England 1-0 in 90', Under 2.5, BTTS-No.
_postmatch.grade: ❌ MISS on the binding call -- the committed side (England) was eliminated, and both committed markets broke (2-1 = Over-adjacent 3 goals vs Under 2.5; BTTS-Yes vs BTTS-No). Full transparency: the VOIDED original call (issued on my estimated line, then withdrawn when the real Bet365 board arrived) was 'Argentina 2-1 in 90', Over 2.5, BTTS-Yes' -- the EXACT result, a would-have-been 🎯 bullseye. The re-issue flipped a bullseye into a miss.
_postmatch.verdict: The most instructive game of the tournament for the METHOD. What happened: my measured evidence (ratings, profiles: Argentina 3 goals in every knockout, England BTTS-Yes in 5 of 7) said Argentina 2-1; the real Bet365 line said England thin-favourite in a cagey Under game; per the alignment discipline I capitulated to the market -- and the market was WRONG on both side and texture, while my recorded DISSENT ('both profiles argue for more goals; if it opens up, the Under/BTTS-No legs break first') was exactly right. Two readings, both true: (1) the real-odds rule remains CORRECT -- estimated lines are circular and asking for the board was right; (2) but WHICH market matters: a single recreational UK book on an ENGLAND game carries documented home-country bias (England shortened by betting volume, not information). I flagged that bias when the screenshot arrived and then failed to act on my own flag -- full capitulation to a biased single-book line, against a validated 7-match evidence base, was the error. The market is a control, not an oracle.
_postmatch.lesson: REFINEMENT to the real-odds rule (do NOT revert it -- refine it): (a) real odds are still mandatory as the control; (b) but calibrate DEFERENCE to the SOURCE -- a sharp book or exchange (Pinnacle, Betfair) earns full alignment; a single recreational book, especially a UK book pricing an England game, earns partial deference: correct the MAGNITUDE toward it, but do not fully flip a side/texture call that a validated evidence base supports -- hold the model view within honest divergence and document the gap; (c) a recorded dissent that strong (profiles 7/7 on goals) should CAP the capitulation -- if I write 'if it opens up the Under legs break first', the bottom line should not be Under. Do not over-learn either (n=1): the Spain lesson (don't fade the elite favourite) came from cases where the market was right about FAVOURITES; this case is about a near-coin-flip where one biased book flipped the side. Argentina profile now 4-for-4 (scored 2-3, conceded, won in 90' this time). FINAL: Spain (GA 2 in 8, six clean sheets) vs Argentina (goals chaos, 4 straight knockout wins) -- the ultimate defence-vs-chaos texture clash.
